UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a customer or admin user of the Frewsie Shop platform. This entity stores user-specific data relevant to the application, excluding authentication credentials which are managed by an external system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: Email address of the user, used for communication and identification.

phone.description: Phone number of the user, used for contact and delivery purposes.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a product category, used to organize and classify products within the Frewsie Shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

image.description: URL to an image that visually represents the category.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the category was created.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a single product available for purchase in the Frewsie Shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

slug.description: A URL-friendly, unique string identifier for the product, often used in product page URLs.

description.description: Detailed description of the product, including features and specifications.

price.description: The regular selling price of the product.

discountPrice.description: The discounted selling price of the product, if it's currently on sale.

categoryId.description: Reference to the Category this product belongs to. (Relationship: Category 1:N Product)

images.description: An array of URLs to various images of the product.

stock.description: The current quantity of the product available in stock.

tags.description: An array of keywords or tags associated with the product for search, filtering, and categorization.

isFlashSale.description: A boolean flag indicating if the product is currently part of a flash sale.

flashSaleEndTime.description: Timestamp indicating when the flash sale for this product is scheduled to end. Only relevant if 'isFlashSale' is true.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the product was first added to the inventory.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the product's information was updated.

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a customer's confirmed purchase order within the Frewsie Shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who placed this order. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Order)

items.description: An array of product items included in this order, capturing their state at the time of purchase.

subtotal.description: The sum of prices of all items in the order before any discounts are applied.

discount.description: The total monetary value of discounts applied to this order.

total.description: The final total price of the order after all discounts and before any payment processing fees.

paymentStatus.description: The current payment status of the order (e.g., 'pending', 'paid', 'failed', 'refunded').

deliveryStatus.description: The current delivery status of the order (e.g., 'pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled').

deliveryDetails.description: Details pertaining to the delivery of the order, including recipient information and address.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the order was placed.

definition.description: Stores individual customer orders. Nested under the user's path, this ensures that the `userId` is denormalized directly into the path for authorization independence. The `userId` field within the document also redundantly matches the path's `userId` for robust security rules. Customers can only read/write their own orders.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who placed the order, matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific order.

definition.description: A dedicated collection to store Admin roles based on Database Access Control (DBAC). Each document's ID (`adminUid`) corresponds to a Firebase `uid` that possesses administrative privileges. This design allows for authorization checks using `exists()` without relying on custom claims or hierarchical `get()` calls, enhancing security rule clarity and debuggability. The schema for this entity is implied and would typically contain minimal data like `{ role: 'admin', createdAt: timestamp }`.

params.name: adminUid
params.description: The unique user ID of an administrator.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Frewsie Shop prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable access control by strictly adhering to the core design principles. This is achieved primarily through a combination of structural segregation and strategic denormalization.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
1.  **User-Owned Data:** For entities like `UserProfile` and `Order`, the structure employs hierarchical paths: `/users/{userId}` and `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}`. This design inherently denormalizes the `userId` into the document path. Consequently, security rules can evaluate ownership directly by comparing `request.auth.uid` with the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, eliminating the need for expensive and potentially inconsistent `get()` calls to parent documents or other collections to determine authorization. This enables atomic operations (e.g., creating a user profile and their first order in a single batch) without breaking security rule evaluation.
2.  **Global Roles (DBAC):** For admin roles, authorization is decoupled from user profiles by using a dedicated top-level collection: `/admin_roles/{adminUid}`. An `exists()` check on this collection (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admin_roles/$(request.auth.uid))`) provides a clear and atomic way to grant admin privileges without requiring `get()` calls on potentially complex user documents.

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
1.  **Public Data:** `categories` and `products` are placed in top-level collections (`/categories/{categoryId}`, `/products/{productId}`). All documents within these collections share the same security posture: public read access for all users (authenticated or unauthenticated) and admin-only write access. This simplifies security rules immensely, as there's no mixed-access data requiring complex conditional logic within a single collection.
2.  **Private User Data:** `UserProfile` and `Order` data are segregated under user-specific paths (`/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}`). This ensures that only the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`) can access their specific data, preventing unauthorized reads or writes.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **Public Collections:** For `categories` and `products`, a `list` operation will return all accessible documents because all documents in these collections are publicly readable. The rules explicitly grant `read` access for all, fulfilling the Query As a Permission (QAP) principle without requiring client-side filtering.
2.  **User-Owned Collections:** For `orders`, the path `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}` combined with the rule `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;` ensures that a `list` query on `/users/$(request.auth.uid)/orders` will *only* return the authenticated user's orders. The database itself enforces this permission, guaranteeing that the client only receives data it is authorized to see, thus upholding the QAP principle.

**Invariants:** Timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`), ownership (`userId` in path and document for orders), and explicit state (`isFlashSale`, `paymentStatus`, `deliveryStatus`) are clearly defined in the schemas, allowing rules to enforce their integrity (e.g., `createdAt` can only be set on create, `updatedAt` on update, `userId` matches `request.auth.uid`).
